title: KS distance
prompt: Write ks(a,b) for two nonempty numeric lists. Compare ECDFs at every distinct observed value. Example: [1,2] versus [2,3] gives .5.
solution:
def ks(a,b):
    return max(abs(sum(x<=t for x in a)/len(a)-sum(x<=t for x in b)/len(b)) for t in set(a+b))
tests:
assert ks([1,2],[2,3])==.5, 'Largest cumulative gap is .5'
assert ks([1,1],[1,1])==0, 'Identical tied distributions have distance zero'
assert ks([0,0],[1,1])==1, 'Disjoint ordered samples have distance one'
hint: The CDF includes observations equal to t.

title: Ranking AUC with ties
prompt: Write auc(positive,negative) for nonempty score lists. Give each positive-negative pair 1 for greater, .5 for equal, else 0. Example: [.5] versus [.5] gives .5.
solution:
def auc(positive,negative):
    return sum((p>n)+.5*(p==n) for p in positive for n in negative)/(len(positive)*len(negative))
tests:
assert auc([.5],[.5])==.5, 'Tied scores earn half credit'
assert auc([.8,.5],[.5,.2])==.875, 'Count all positive-negative pairs'
assert auc([0],[1])==0 and auc([1],[0])==1, 'Keep the positive-score orientation'
hint: Divide by the number of pairs.
